title: Distributed Matrix-Based Sampling for Graph Neural Network Training
problem: GNN training on large graphs requires sampling subgraphs or nodes to manage memory and computation, but coordinating sampling across distributed nodes introduces synchronization overhead and communication bottlenecks.
motivation: Efficient distributed sampling is critical for scaling GNN training to graphs with billions of nodes and edges.
method: The approach formulates node/edge sampling for GNN training as matrix operations, enabling efficient computation of sampling probabilities in distributed settings. It coordinates sampling decisions across multiple devices using matrix-based representations to reduce per-step communication and leverage GPU/CPU matrix multiplication capabilities.
key_novelty: Using matrix-based formulations to unify and optimize sampling operations in distributed GNN training.
contributions: Matrix-based sampling framework for distributed GNN training
Distributed coordination mechanism reducing communication overhead
Empirical validation showing improved training throughput and scalability
Analysis of sampling bias and convergence in distributed settings

metrics.speedup: distributed training speedup relative to baseline

limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in title-only analysis.
primary_theme: matrix-based sampling for distributed GNN training
